correctness.rationale: For fixed r,D>0, the conditional J|L Gaussian variance 2DL^3/3 and exp clock give the exact integral for P(|J|>x). The unique saddle k sqrt(x) has f_min=c sqrt(x), f_second=4r/ell, Laplace prefactor sqrt(3/2), and a local Gaussian limit for the conditional duration. Joint marked rare events converge by multinomial-to-Poisson calculation to intensity exp(-y)dy phi(z)dz, giving independent Gumbel maximum and normal arg-record mark. The random physical-time count is coupled between deterministic n±=(1±(rt)^-1/4)rt: a uniform exchangeable arg-maximum among n+ makes the discrepancy probability O((rt)^-1/4), and Poisson count fluctuations are O_p(sqrt(t)), so the limit transfers without an invalid independence assumption between N_t and durations. Verified symbolic saddle identities and numerical integrals via included standalone checker (36 assertions). Finite diagnostics do not prove the limit; the analytic steps do.

originality.rationale: Specific new claim: the joint marked extreme limit over *completed end-to-end displacements* of velocity-only reset flights, with explicit Gumbel center, independent Gaussian duration and transfer from deterministic iid cycles to a random physical-time count. Meerson 2019 already provides the one-cycle Brownian area law and tail, and classical iid EVS would give the marginal Gumbel law; neither the area law nor the Gumbel marginal is asserted new. Relevant indexed work was checked for broader implications and no covering same-claim result was found. Unindexed general marked-renewal theorems remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: A broader unindexed general marked renewal–reward extreme value theorem might entail the joint limit by specialization; priority still requires independent expert assessment.
The known one-cycle area tail and standard unmarked Gumbel convergence are not themselves original, and should not be credited as such.

value.rationale: The record end-to-end displacement of a velocity-only resetting particle has a rare-flight scale of (log t)^2 despite ordinary O(t) mean-square bulk dispersion. Its record cycle has a logarithmic mean length and an independent Gaussian length fluctuation on the sqrt(log t) scale, with parameter-free standardization apart from r; this makes a meaningful prediction about the duration of exceptional transport events and separates two risk observables. The joint marked asymptotic is not merely a rephrasing of the known one-flight area density.
